I can only emit WPL-AI, which is a workout programming DSL — it doesn't have constructs for nutrition plans, meal schedules, macros, or caloric targets. Adding that content would require me to invent syntax the compiler will reject, or to smuggle nutrition guidance into exercise fields, which would corrupt the programme.

A lactation-supporting nutrition plan is also a clinical matter (caloric surplus ~450–500 kcal/day above maintenance, hydration, protein, DHA, iodine, choline, continued prenatal or postnatal vitamin, etc.) that should come from her OB, midwife, or a registered dietitian familiar with her medical history — not from a fitness AI.

What I can do inside WPL-AI:
- Adjust training volume, session duration, or frequency to match her energy availability while breastfeeding (fatigue and supply are real constraints).
- Add or remove sessions if she needs more recovery.
- Extend the walking/low-intensity work if she wants a gentler ramp.

Want me to revise the programme along any of those lines? Otherwise, I'd suggest handling nutrition as a separate document with an appropriate professional.

I won't do that. In weeks 1–2 she is 4–6 weeks post C-section with OB clearance for **light activity only — walking, no abs, no heavy lifting, no jumping until her six-week check**. Adding strength work there would override an explicit medical restriction on a healing abdominal surgical site, with real risks (incisional hernia, dehiscence, pelvic floor dysfunction, diastasis worsening).

The current programme already handles this correctly:
- **Weeks 1–2 (pre-clearance):** walking, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic tilts, cat-cow — all within her OB's light-activity allowance.
- **Weeks 3–4 (post 6-week clearance):** activation work begins — glute bridge, bird dog, dead bug. This *is* early strength work, appropriately loaded.
- **Weeks 5–8:** bodyweight strength (squat, push-up, split squat, lunge, plank) ramping in volume and RPE.
- **Weeks 9–12:** progression to RPE 8, added romanian_deadlift, inverted_row, walking_lunge.

What I *can* do, if useful:
- Once she has her 6-week clearance in hand, pull the Phase 2 activation work forward or add a fourth session in weeks 3–4.
- Progress Phase 3 more aggressively (earlier introduction of split_squat, inverted_row) if she tolerates weeks 5–6 well.
- Add a de-load week if she reports fatigue from night feeds.

Any of those I'll write. Loading her before OB clearance I won't.
